$comment: Skin structures and where their geometry comes from. bp3d: BodyParts3D 4.0 part ids (Human Atlas build). modelled: built in code by tools/make-skin.mjs from the dimensions in provenance.json.

structures.note: BodyParts3D skin surface, welded and simplified to about 28,000 triangles; per-vertex rule-of-nines region and dermatome labels added.

structures.modelled: Anucleate keratinised squames: 18 µm on thin skin, 400 µm on thick skin; the surface carries polygonal creases (thin) and friction ridges 0.46 mm apart (thick), with pores and the follicular ostium.
Clear eosinophilic band of thick skin only, 35 µm, fading out at the thin–thick boundary.
Keratohyalin-granule layer, 8 µm (1–2 cells) on thin skin to 35 µm on thick skin.
Prickle-cell layer: fills the rete ridges between the dermal papillae; flat on top, following the basal layer below.
One cell (11–16 µm) on the basement membrane, following every papilla.
Dendritic pigment cells on the basement membrane, dendrites reaching up between keratinocytes; 3084 instances (about 1 in 7 of the real ~1,000–1,500 per mm²; fewer on palms).
Dendritic antigen-presenting cells in the spinous layer, dendrites spread between keratinocytes; 1675 instances (about 1 in 7 of the real ~460–1,000 per mm²).

Loose connective tissue of the dermal papillae and the band beneath; thin skin: low papillae ~0.06 mm high about 0.1 mm apart; thick skin: double rows of papillae between primary and secondary rete ridges.
Dense irregular connective tissue down to 2.05 mm (thin) / 3.05 mm (thick) below the surface; fat domes rise into its base.
49 representative type I collagen bundles (~45–60 µm) interwoven in layers roughly parallel to the surface (real bundles are far more numerous; the reticular dermis texture shows the rest).
Adipose tissue from the dermis to the deep fascia at 5.25 mm.
Connective-tissue septa (retinacula cutis) ~0.1 mm thick dividing the fat into lobules ~1.5 mm across; Voronoi faces of jittered seeds, warped.
Investing deep fascia, 0.28 mm.
Terminal hair 72 µm thick (cuticle, cortex, medulla not separated), from the keratogenous zone above the papilla to 1.7 mm beyond the skin, leaning with the follicle (55° to the surface).
Henle and Huxley layers and cuticle (not separated): 14 µm thick around the shaft, from the bulb to the isthmus.
Outer root sheath with the glassy membrane and connective-tissue sheath (~65 µm), continuous with the epidermis at the infundibulum (ostium ~0.18 mm).
Hair bulb ~0.34 mm across: the matrix (with melanocytes) cupped around the dermal papilla, at the dermis–hypodermis junction (anagen terminal follicle).
Dermal (hair) papilla: a pear-shaped knot of specialised fibroblasts and capillaries, ~0.14 × 0.28 mm, with its stalk joining the connective-tissue sheath.
Smooth-muscle bundle ~80 µm thick from the follicle bulge to the papillary dermis, on the obtuse-angle side; it fans into three slips at its upper end.
Holocrine gland of four acini (~0.25–0.3 mm) in the angle between the follicle and the arrector pili; its short duct opens into the follicle canal ~0.5 mm below the surface.

Four merocrine sweat glands (one thin-skin, three thick-skin; real density 100–600 per cm²): secretory coil ~0.3–0.4 mm in the deep dermis, a straight dermal duct to the tip of a rete ridge, and a spiral intra-epidermal duct (acrosyringium) to a pore — on a ridge crest in thick skin. Tubules hollow, ~50 µm across.

Apocrine gland of axillary type: a coil ~0.8 mm across of wide tubules (~120 µm, large lumen) at the dermis–hypodermis junction; its duct opens into the follicle infundibulum above the sebaceous duct.
12 encapsulated corpuscles ~45 × 95 µm in the dermal papillae of thick skin: stacked flattened lamellar (Schwann) cells with the axon winding between them, long axis perpendicular to the surface.

Merkel cell–neurite complexes in the basal layer: a row at the tip of a primary rete ridge (thick skin) and a touch dome beside the hair (thin skin). Each: a Merkel cell over a disc-shaped Aβ terminal; drawn ×1.3 so they show at block scale.

Two lamellated corpuscles (~1.0 × 0.6 and 0.8 × 0.5 mm) in the subcutaneous fat: concentric lamellae (6 and 5 drawn; real corpuscles have 20–60) with fluid between them, round an inner core holding the unmyelinated axon terminal.
Two spindle-shaped Ruffini endings (~0.76 × 0.08 mm) in the reticular dermis, aligned with the collagen; branched terminals among the collagen fibres at each pole.

34 thin (Aδ and C) fibres from the subepidermal plexus that lose their Schwann cells at the basement membrane and end among the keratinocytes up to the granular layer; drawn ~8 µm thick (real 0.5–2 µm) so they show.
Lanceolate endings (palisade parallel to the follicle) and circumferential fibres around the follicle at the level of the bulge, below the sebaceous gland.

Subpapillary (superficial) plexus at the papillary–reticular junction: arterioles (~20 µm, red) with paired, slightly deeper venules (~28 µm, blue); 218 capillary loops (~9 µm) rise into the dermal papillae (shown in the papillae near the standard sections and a sample elsewhere).

Deep (cutaneous) plexus at the dermis–hypodermis junction: arterioles ~60 µm and venules ~90 µm; communicating (candelabra) vessels up to the superficial plexus; a perforating artery and vein through the deep fascia; branches to the hair papilla, the sweat-gland coils and the fat lobules.

Blind-ended initial lymphatics in the papillary dermis drain to a superficial lymphatic plexus below the venous plexus; valved (beaded) collectors run down through the dermis to a deep plexus and out beside the perforating vessels.

A cutaneous nerve (~145 µm) in the subcutaneous fat; ascending branches form the subepidermal plexus and supply the Meissner, Merkel, Ruffini and Pacinian endings and the follicle plexus; fine sympathetic fibres reach the arrector pili and the sweat glands.
